subject: merge-sort

composition.story: Start with an unsorted list, then split it into single-item runs. Merge sorted runs by repeatedly taking their smaller front item. Watch the final output grow while remaining sorted; when one run empties, append the other. Use Previous and Next to inspect each choice.

aha.observation: Choosing the smaller front of two sorted runs preserves output order; repeated merges therefore sort the entire list.

states.label: Unsorted input
states.sentence: Begin with the fixed unsorted input.
states.why: The Input is unsorted; splitting creates smaller sorting problems without changing any values.

states.label: Split into halves
states.sentence: Divide the Input into Left half and Right half.
states.why: Both halves preserve input order; each must be split again before merging.

states.label: Reach singletons
states.sentence: Split each half into singleton runs.
states.why: Every singleton is already sorted, giving merge sort its base case.

states.label: Merge left pair
states.sentence: Merge the left singleton pair into a sorted run.
states.why: Compare the singleton fronts, place the smaller first, then append the remaining singleton.

states.label: Merge right pair
states.sentence: Merge the right singleton pair into a sorted run.
states.why: The same rule creates the Right sorted run; both runs are now ready for the final merge.

states.label: Choose right front
states.sentence: Compare both run fronts and start the output with the smaller.
states.why: The right front is smaller; choosing it starts a sorted output prefix.

states.label: Choose left front
states.sentence: Advance the right front and compare again.
states.why: Skip the consumed right first cell; the left front is now smaller, preserving output order.

states.label: Choose right remainder
states.sentence: Compare the remaining fronts and extend the sorted prefix.
states.why: Skip both consumed first cells; the right front is smaller, so the output remains sorted.

states.label: Append and finish
states.sentence: The output contains every input item in nondecreasing order.
states.why: The right run is empty; append the left remainder without comparing, completing the sorted output.
